title: Steady applications, falling loan revenue
disclaimer: Practice scenario. The company is fictional and every figure is hypothetical. Australian market context is general.
company_context: LendLeaf (fictional) is an Australian digital lender offering unsecured personal loans through its app and a broker channel.

brief.problem: Personal loan revenue is falling even though application numbers are steady.
brief.objective: Bring funded loan volume back to $45m a month within six months.
baseline: Funded loans: $31m a month, down from $45m.

facts.answer: Net interest margin plus fees averages about 6% a year on funded balances. The $14m monthly shortfall means about $840k less annual revenue for every month it continues.
facts.coach_tip: Say the 'so what': every month of lost volume locks in a year of lost revenue.
facts.model_question: What's the revenue impact of the funded volume drop?

facts.answer: Funded volume is the total paid out to customers in the month. An application counts once it's submitted with ID. The funded rate has fallen from 42% of applications to 29%.
facts.coach_tip: Volume fell while applications held, so look at conversion, not demand.
facts.model_question: How are funded volume and conversion measured?

facts.answer: Self-employed applicants: funded rate fell from 31% to 12%. PAYG employees: from 46% to 35%. Self-employed make up about a quarter of applications.
facts.coach_tip: Both fell, but self-employed collapsed — name both.
facts.model_question: Which applicant segments are converting worse?

facts.answer: Approved applicants who don't draw down: 9%, unchanged. Average loan size is steady at about $18,000.
facts.coach_tip: Loss isn't after approval — it's earlier.
facts.model_question: Are approved customers taking smaller loans or not drawing down?

facts.answer: Submitted 100% → identity verified 95% → income verified 52% (was 81%) → credit approved 31% → funded 29%.
facts.coach_tip: The biggest drop is income verification: 81% to 52%.
facts.model_question: Can I see the application funnel and where it drops?

facts.answer: 88% of applications come through the mobile app and 12% through brokers. The broker funded rate is steady at 47%.
facts.coach_tip: Brokers are fine — the issue is in the app journey.
facts.model_question: Does the drop differ by channel?

facts.answer: Four months ago, income verification moved from uploading payslips or tax returns to linking bank accounts via Open Banking (CDR) only. Uploads were removed to cut manual review costs.
facts.coach_tip: Link this to the verification drop and the self-employed collapse.
facts.model_question: Did anything change in income verification?

facts.answer: Drop-off survey: my bank isn't supported or wouldn't connect 36%, didn't want to share bank data 29%, self-employed income looked wrong 22%. Complaints about declined loans doubled.
facts.coach_tip: 65% cite bank-linking problems — that's your target.
facts.model_question: What do applicants who drop out tell us?

facts.answer: Our rates rose 0.25 points in the same period. Competitor rates rose by a similar amount.
facts.coach_tip: Market-wide, so it doesn't explain our drop.
facts.model_question: Could rates or competitors explain this?

facts.answer: The manual review team was cut from 10 to 4 people, saving about $450k a year.
facts.coach_tip: The saving is real, but much smaller than the revenue lost.
facts.model_question: What did the change save in operations?

facts.answer: Estimates: bring back document upload as a fallback — 3 weeks plus about 2 reviewers ($180k a year). Accountant-prepared statements for self-employed — 5 weeks. A second CDR provider to cover more banks — 7 weeks.
facts.coach_tip: Weigh $180k a year against $840k of revenue per month of lost volume.
facts.model_question: What are our options and estimates?

model_answer.problem_statement: App applicants, especially the self-employed, are dropping out at income verification — the pass rate fell from 81% to 52% — because uploads were removed and bank-linking via CDR fails or puts people off, cutting funded loans from $45m to $31m a month.

options.name: Upload fallback
options.description: Bring back payslip and tax return uploads when bank-linking fails or is declined.
options.business_impact: Targets 65% of drop-outs; could restore most of the $14m a month for $180k a year.
options.why: Fastest, biggest recovery for the cost.

options.name: Self-employed statements
options.description: Accept accountant-prepared income statements for self-employed applicants.
options.business_impact: Helps the 22% whose income looked wrong.

options.name: Second CDR provider
options.description: Add another provider to cover more banks.
options.business_impact: Helps the 36% whose bank failed; not those who won't share data.

model_answer.decision: Restore document upload as a fallback within 3 weeks, staffed by 2 reviewers, and add a second CDR provider next quarter to shrink manual reviews over time.
model_answer.hypothesis: If we restore document upload as a fallback when bank-linking fails or is declined, income verification will rise from 52% to 75% and funded volume from $31m to $42m a month within one quarter, because the drop started when uploads were removed and 65% of drop-outs cite bank-linking problems.
model_answer.test: A/B test app applicants: fallback upload vs CDR-only for 4 weeks.
